code:
module xor_nn (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [1:0] x, // 2 inputs for XOR
    output reg y // output for XOR
);
    reg [7:0] w1_1, w1_2; // weights from input to hidden layer
    reg [7:0] w2; // weight from hidden to output layer
    reg [7:0] h1, h2; // hidden layer outputs
    reg [7:0] output_layer; // final output
    reg [7:0] learning_rate = 8'd5; // learning rate
    reg [7:0] loss;

    // weight initialization
    initial begin
        w1_1 = 8'd10; // weight from input 1 to hidden 1
        w1_2 = 8'd10; // weight from input 2 to hidden 1
        w2 = 8'd10; // weight from hidden 1 to output
    end
    
    // Forward propagation
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            y <= 0;
        end else begin
            h1 = (x[0] * w1_1 + x[1] * w1_2) >> 4; // simple activation
            output_layer = (h1 * w2) >> 4; // output calculation
            y <= output_layer[0]; // output for XOR
        end
    end
    
    // Backpropagation
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (!rst) begin
            loss = (y ^ (x[0] ^ x[1])); // XOR target value
            w2 = w2 - (learning_rate * loss * h1) >> 4; // update output weight
            w1_1 = w1_1 - (learning_rate * loss * x[0]) >> 4; // update hidden weight 1
            w1_2 = w1_2 - (learning_rate * loss * x[1]) >> 4; // update hidden weight 2
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire [7:0] data_in, // 8-bit data to be transmitted
    input wire start,         // Signal to start transmission
    input wire stop,          // Signal to stop transmission
    input wire baud_tick,     // Tick signal for baud rate
    output reg tx             // Serial output
);

    reg [10:0] shift_reg;      // Shift register to hold the complete frame (start + data + stop)
    reg transmitting;          // Status of transmission

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            tx <= 1;           // Idle state of UART
            transmitting <= 0;
            bit_counter <= 0;
        end else if (start && !transmitting) begin
            // Load the shift register with start bit, data bits, and stop bit
            shift_reg <= {1'b1, data_in, 1'b0}; // Start, Data, Stop
            transmitting <= 1;
            bit_counter <= 0;
        end else if (transmitting) begin
            if (baud_tick) begin
                tx <= shift_reg[0]; // Output the least significant bit
                shift_reg <= shift_reg >> 1; // Shift right
                bit_counter <= bit_counter + 1;
                if (bit_counter == 10) begin
                    transmitting <= 0; // Transmission complete
                end
            end
        end
    end

The input message is provided in blocks of 512 bits, and the hash output is generated after processing each block.

Design a simple memory allocator and deallocator in Verilog that simulates the malloc and free functionalities. The memory should be represented as a register array, and the system should keep track of allocated and freed blocks. The system should have inputs for requesting memory size and a free signal to release allocated memory. The output should indicate the starting address of the allocated block or a failure if there is not enough memory available.

Calculate the IP checksum for a given 16-bit words input. The checksum is computed as the one's complement of the sum of all 16-bit words. The input will be a sequence of 16-bit words, and the output will be a single 16-bit checksum value.

Design a 5-bit ring counter in Verilog that cycles through a sequence of states where only one bit is high at any time. The counter should reset to 00001 when a reset signal is applied. The counter should increment on each clock cycle.
code:
module ring_counter (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    output reg [4:0] count
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset)
            count <= 5'b00001; // Initialize to 00001 on reset
        else
            count <= {count[3:0], count[4]}; // Shift left and wrap around
    end
endmodule

description:
Implement a simple matrix factorization function that takes two 4x4 matrices (A and B) as input and produces their product matrix (C). The multiplication of two matrices can be defined as:

C[i][j] = Σ (A[i][k] * B[k][j]) for k = 0 to 3

Your task is to write the Verilog code that performs this computation for 4x4 matrices.

Implement a simple I2C master controller that generates the start condition, stop condition, and sends data to a slave device. The controller should accept a 7-bit address and 8-bit data input, and output the signals for SCL and SDA.

Design a packet filtering module for a simple firewall that checks incoming packets against a set of rules. Each packet has a source IP address (32 bits), destination IP address (32 bits), and a protocol type (8 bits). The module should output "ALLOW" or "BLOCK" based on whether the packet matches the defined rules. The rules are stored in a 2D array (up to 4 rules, where each rule consists of source IP, destination IP, and protocol type). The module should output "ALLOW" if a matching rule is found, otherwise "BLOCK".
code:
module packet_filter (
    input [31:0] src_ip,
    input [31:0] dest_ip,
    input [7:0] protocol,
    output reg [7:0] action
);
    reg [31:0] rules_src [0:3]; // Source IP rules
    reg [31:0] rules_dest [0:3]; // Destination IP rules
    reg [7:0] rules_proto [0:3]; // Protocol rules
    integer i;

    initial begin
        // Example rules
        rules_src[0] = 32'hC0A80001; // 192.168.0.1
        rules_dest[0] = 32'hC0A80002; // 192.168.0.2
        rules_proto[0] = 8'h06; // TCP

        rules_src[1] = 32'hC0A80003; // 192.168.0.3
        rules_dest[1] = 32'hC0A80004; // 192.168.0.4
        rules_proto[1] = 8'h11; // UDP

        // Other rules can be added similarly
        // Here we consider two rules for simplicity
    end

    always @(*) begin
        action = "BLOCK"; // Default action
        for (i = 0; i < 2; i = i + 1) begin
            if (src_ip == rules_src[i] && dest_ip == rules_dest[i] && protocol == rules_proto[i]) begin
                action = "ALLOW"; // Match found
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple 2-input multiplexer (MUX) that selects one of the two inputs based on a select signal. The output should be the selected input.

Design a LIFO stack using Verilog. The stack should support push and pop operations. The design should include a 4-bit data input, a push and pop control signal, and a 3-bit stack pointer to track the top of the stack. Implement the necessary logic to handle overflow and underflow conditions.

Design a simple Kalman filter module that estimates the state of a system based on noisy measurements. The module should take the current measurement input, the predicted state, and the covariance matrix as inputs, and produce an updated state and covariance matrix as outputs.
Design a LIFO stack in Verilog that supports push, pop, and peek operations. The stack should have a fixed depth and should provide a status output indicating whether the stack is full or empty.

Design a fan speed control system that adjusts the fan speed based on the temperature levels. The fan has three speed settings: low, medium, and high. The system takes a 2-bit input representing temperature levels, where 00 = low, 01 = medium, 10 = high, and 11 = off. The output is a 2-bit representation of the fan speed settings: 00 = off, 01 = low, 10 = medium, and 11 = high. The fan speed should only change when the temperature input changes.
code:
module fan_speed_control (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [1:0] temp,
    output reg [1:0] fan_speed
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            fan_speed <= 2'b00; // off
        end else begin
            case (temp)
                2'b00: fan_speed <= 2'b01; // low
                2'b01: fan_speed <= 2'b10; // medium
                2'b10: fan_speed <= 2'b11; // high
                2'b11: fan_speed <= 2'b00; // off
                default: fan_speed <= 2'b00; // default to off
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple audio mixer that takes in two audio signals (each 8 bits wide) and produces a mixed output signal. The mixed output signal should be the average of the two input signals. The outputs should also be 8 bits wide, with any overflow wrapped around (i.e., using modulo 256 arithmetic).
code:
module audio_mixer (
    input [7:0] signal1,
    input [7:0] signal2,
    output [7:0] mixed_signal
);
    assign mixed_signal = (signal1 + signal2) >> 1; // Average of the two signals
endmodule

description: Design an Adaptive LMS (Least Mean Squares) filter using Verilog. The filter should have inputs for the desired signal, input signal, step size, and a predefined filter order. The output should be the filtered signal. Implement the adaptive adjustment of the filter coefficients based on the LMS algorithm.

K-means clustering involves assigning points to the nearest cluster centers. This problem requires you to implement a combinational logic circuit that determines the nearest cluster center for a given data point based on Euclidean distance. Your circuit should take the coordinates of the data point and the coordinates of two cluster centers as inputs, and output the index of the nearest cluster center (either 0 or 1).

Design a 4x Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) in Verilog that generates an output clock signal that is 4 times the frequency of the input clock signal. The PLL should have an enable signal to start or stop the PLL operation.
code:
module pll_4x (
    input wire clk_in,
    input wire reset,
    input wire enable,
    output reg clk_out
);
    reg [1:0] counter; // 2-bit counter for dividing the input clock

    always @(posedge clk_in or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 2'b00;
            clk_out <= 0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            counter <= counter + 1;
            if (counter == 2'b11) begin
                clk_out <= ~clk_out; // Toggle output clock every 4 input clock cycles
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 4-point FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) module in Verilog. The module should take 4 complex inputs, each represented by 8-bit real and imaginary parts, and compute the 4-point FFT. The output should be 4 complex values, also represented by 8-bit real and imaginary parts.

Design a simple PCIe interface state machine that controls the data transfer process. The state machine transitions between three states: IDLE, TRANSFER, and DONE. The state machine should start in the IDLE state, move to the TRANSFER state upon receiving a start signal, and return to the IDLE state after completing the transfer when a done signal is received.

Design a 2-bit barrel shifter that can shift a 2-bit input either left or right based on a control signal. The barrel shifter should take a 2-bit input and a 1-bit control signal. If the control signal is 0, the output should be the input shifted to the left by 1. If the control signal is 1, the output should be the input shifted to the right by 1. The output should also wrap around for shifts.
code:
module barrel_shifter(
    input [1:0] data_in,
    input ctrl,
    output reg [1:0] data_out
);
    always @(*) begin
        case (ctrl)
            1'b0: data_out = {data_in[0], data_in[1]}; // Left shift
            1'b1: data_out = {data_in[1], data_in[0]}; // Right shift
            default: data_out = 2'b00; // Default case (should not happen)
        endcase
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple EEPROM cell that can store one bit of data. The cell has inputs for setting the data (D), a write enable (WE), and a read enable (RE). When WE is high, the data input D is written to the memory cell. When RE is high, the stored data is outputted. The output should be high impedance when not reading or writing.
code:
module eeprom_cell (
    input wire D,
    input wire WE,
    input wire RE,
    output reg Q,
    output wire Z
);
    assign Z = (RE) ? Q : 1'bz; // High impedance when not reading

    always @ (posedge WE) begin
        if (WE) begin
            Q <= D; // Store data when write enable is high
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a linear voltage regulator in Verilog that takes a 5-bit binary input voltage (0 to 31) and produces a regulated output voltage which is a scaled version of the input. The output should only change on the rising edge of a clock signal and should maintain the last value until the next clock pulse. The scaling factor should be a fixed value, for example, 3 (i.e., output = input * 3). If the output exceeds the maximum value for 5 bits (31), it should be clamped to 31.

Design a 32-point FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) module in Verilog. The module should take a 32-bit input signal and produce a 32-bit output signal representing the FFT result. The FFT should be implemented using a simple radix-2 algorithm, and the module should support a clock signal for synchronization.

Design a fractional-N Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) in Verilog. The PLL should take a reference clock input and a frequency divider value as inputs. The PLL should produce an output clock with a frequency that is a fractional multiple of the input reference clock frequency. The design should include a phase detector, a loop filter, and a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO).

Design a UART transmitter module in Verilog. The UART transmitter should take an 8-bit data input, a transmit enable signal, and output a serial data stream at a specified baud rate. The module should also generate a start bit, data bits, and a stop bit. The module should handle the baud rate generation using a simple counter.

Create a Wallace tree multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers A and B. The output should be a 8-bit binary result. Implement the multiplier using a hierarchical structure with partial products and final summation.

Design a Fractional-N PLL controller that takes an input frequency and generates a divided output frequency using a fractional value. The design should include a simple state machine that toggles between different states based on the input frequency.

Design a 16-bit deserializer that converts a serial input into a parallel 16-bit output. The deserializer should take a clock signal and a serial input signal. On each clock cycle, a new bit from the serial input is captured, and after 16 clock cycles, the parallel output is ready.

Design a Kogge-Stone adder in Verilog that takes two n-bit binary numbers as input and outputs their sum. The Kogge-Stone adder is a parallel prefix adder that uses a tree structure to compute the carry bits efficiently.

Design a 16-bit SRAM cell that can store a value and be read from. The SRAM cell should have the following inputs: an address (4 bits), a write enable signal (we), a data input (16 bits), and a data output (16 bits). When the write enable signal is asserted, the data input should be stored at the specified address. When the write enable signal is not asserted, the data output should reflect the value stored at the specified address.
code:
module sram_cell (
    input wire [3:0] addr,
    input wire we,
    input wire [15:0] data_in,
    output reg [15:0] data_out
);
    reg [15:0] memory [0:15]; // 16 x 16-bit memory

    always @(posedge we) begin
        if (we) begin
            memory[addr] <= data_in; // Write data
        end
    end

    always @(*) begin
        data_out = memory[addr]; // Read data
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that implements bilinear interpolation for a 2x2 pixel image. The inputs to the module will be four pixel values (A, B, C, D) and two interpolation factors (u, v) which will range from 0 to 1 (using fixed-point representation). The output should be the interpolated pixel value.
code:
module bilinear_interpolation (
    input [7:0] A, // pixel value at (0,0)
    input [7:0] B, // pixel value at (0,1)
    input [7:0] C, // pixel value at (1,0)
    input [7:0] D, // pixel value at (1,1)
    input [7:0] u, // horizontal interpolation factor
    input [7:0] v, // vertical interpolation factor
    output reg [7:0] out // interpolated pixel value
);
    always @(*) begin
        // Calculate the interpolated value
        // Using fixed-point arithmetic: (A * (1-u) * (1-v)) + (B * (1-u) * v) + (C * u * (1-v)) + (D * u * v)
        out = (A * (255-u) * (255-v) + 
               B * (255-u) * v + 
               C * u * (255-v) + 
               D * u * v) >> 16; // Right shift to normalize the result
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 24-bit Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) output controller. The controller takes a 24-bit input, representing the digital signal, and outputs a corresponding 24-bit value. The output should be the same as the input, but it should also include a control signal that indicates whether the output is valid or not. The valid signal is high when the input value is greater than a defined threshold.

Design a simple Network Address Translation (NAT) module that converts a private IP address (32 bits) to a public IP address (32 bits) based on a predefined mapping table. The module should take a private IP address as input and output the corresponding public IP address. If the private IP address is not found in the mapping table, the output should be a default public IP address (e.g., 0.0.0.0).
code:
module nat_ipv4 (
    input [31:0] private_ip,
    output reg [31:0] public_ip
);
    // Predefined mapping table
    reg [31:0] private_table[0:4]; // 5 entries
    reg [31:0] public_table[0:4]; // 5 corresponding public IPs
    integer i;
    initial begin
        // Initialize the mapping table
        private_table[0] = 32'hC0A80101; // 192.168.1.1
        public_table[0] = 32'h0A000001; // 10.0.0.1

        private_table[1] = 32'hC0A80102; // 192.168.1.2
        public_table[1] = 32'h0A000002; // 10.0.0.2

        private_table[2] = 32'hC0A80103; // 192.168.1.3
        public_table[2] = 32'h0A000003; // 10.0.0.3

        private_table[3] = 32'hC0A80104; // 192.168.1.4
        public_table[3] = 32'h0A000004; // 10.0.0.4

        private_table[4] = 32'hC0A80105; // 192.168.1.5
        public_table[4] = 32'h0A000005; // 10.0.0.5
    end

    always @(*) begin
        public_ip = 32'h00000000; // default public IP
        for (i = 0; i < 5; i = i + 1) begin
            if (private_ip == private_table[i]) begin
                public_ip = public_table[i];
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Serial-In Serial-Out (SISO) shift register with a parameterizable width. The shift register should take a serial bit input and shift it into the register on each clock cycle. It should also provide a serial output, which outputs the bits shifted out in the same order they were input. There should be asynchronous reset functionality to initialize the register to zeros.
code:
module SISO_Shift_Register #(
    parameter WIDTH = 5
) (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire serial_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [WIDTH-1:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            shift_reg <= {WIDTH{1'b0}}; // Initialize to zeros
            serial_out <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            serial_out <= shift_reg[0]; // Output the least significant bit
            shift_reg <= {serial_in, shift_reg[WIDTH-1:1]}; // Shift in new bit
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 16-bit data bus multiplexer that takes four 16-bit inputs (A, B, C, D) and selects one of them based on a 2-bit select signal (sel). The output should be a 16-bit bus that reflects the selected input.

Design a simple RNN cell that takes a single input and produces an output based on the previous state. The RNN cell will have the following parameters: input size of 1, hidden state size of 1, and output size of 1. The output is calculated using a simple linear transformation of the input and the previous state, followed by a basic activation (ReLU). The RNN should have a clock input and a reset input to initialize the hidden state.
code:
module simple_rnn (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] x, // input
    output reg [7:0] h   // hidden state (output)
);
    reg [7:0] h_prev; // previous hidden state

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            h <= 8'b0;      // initialize hidden state to 0
            h_prev <= 8'b0; // initialize previous hidden state to 0
        end else begin
            h <= (h_prev + x > 8'b11111111) ? 8'b11111111 : (h_prev + x); // ReLU activation
            h_prev <= h; // update previous hidden state
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design an IIR filter that processes incoming audio samples and outputs filtered samples based on previous samples and previous outputs. The filter has a single input and a single output. The filter will implement a simple first-order IIR filter defined by the equation: 
y[n] = a * x[n] + b * y[n-1], 
where x[n] is the current input sample, y[n] is the current output sample, a and b are fixed coefficients (for simplicity, let a = 0.5 and b = 0.5).
code:
module IIR_Filter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input signed [15:0] x, // input sample
    output reg signed [15:0] y // output sample
);
    parameter a = 16'h8000; // Coefficient a = 0.5 (fixed point)
    parameter b = 16'h8000; // Coefficient b = 0.5 (fixed point)
    
    reg signed [15:0] y_prev; // previous output sample

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            y <= 16'd0;
            y_prev <= 16'd0;
        end else begin
            y <= (a * x + b * y_prev) >>> 15; // Apply the filter formula
            y_prev <= y; // Update previous output
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 2-bit barrel shifter. The barrel shifter should take a 2-bit input and a 1-bit shift control signal. If the shift control signal is 0, the output should be the same as the input. If the shift control signal is 1, the output should be the input shifted to the left by 1 position, wrapping around the bits.
code:
module barrel_shifter(
    input [1:0] in,
    input ctrl,
    output reg [1:0] out
);
    always @(*) begin
        if (ctrl) begin
            out = {in[0], in[1]}; // Shift left and wrap around
        end else begin
            out = in; // No shift
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Create a 16-bit fixed-point multiplier that multiplies two 8-bit signed fixed-point numbers (with 4 bits representing the integer part and 4 bits representing the fractional part). The output should be a 16-bit signed fixed-point number.

Design a simple NVMe controller state machine that transitions between three states: IDLE, BUSY, and DONE. The controller should start in the IDLE state. When a start signal is received, it transitions to the BUSY state. After a certain process (simulated by a clock edge), it should transition to the DONE state and then back to IDLE when another signal is received.

Design a combinational logic circuit that performs linear regression for a set of 5 data points. The circuit should take 10 inputs (x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, y1, y2, y3, y4, y5) representing the x and y coordinates of the data points. It should output the slope (m) and y-intercept (b) of the best-fitting line (y = mx + b) using the least squares method.

Design a simple SPI master controller that transmits data over the SPI interface. It should have an input for the data to be sent, a clock input, a chip select input, and an output for the SPI data line. The transmission should occur on the rising edge of the clock when the chip select is low.
code:
module spi_master (
    input wire clk,
    input wire cs,         // Chip Select
    input wire [7:0] data, // 8-bit data input
    output reg mosi,      // Master Out Slave In
    output reg done       // Transmission complete flag
);

reg [2:0] bit_counter; // Counter for the number of bits sent

always @(posedge clk or negedge cs) begin
    if (!cs) begin
        bit_counter <= 0;   // Reset bit counter when CS is low
        done <= 0;          // Transmission not done
    end else if (bit_counter < 8) begin
        mosi <= data[7 - bit_counter]; // Send MSB first
        bit_counter <= bit_counter + 1;
    end else begin
        done <= 1;          // Indicate transmission is complete
    end
end

endmodule

description: AES is a symmetric encryption algorithm that processes data in blocks. In this problem, you'll design a module that implements a simplified 8-bit AES encryption algorithm. The module should take an 8-bit plaintext input and a corresponding 8-bit key as inputs. The encryption process will consist of a few basic steps: SubBytes, ShiftRows, and MixColumns. For simplicity, you can use a predefined substitution box (S-Box) and fixed transformations. The design should include a clock input and a reset signal to initialize the encryption process.

Design a 2-stage pipeline for a simple 8-bit adder. The first stage will take two 8-bit inputs, A and B, and produce an intermediate result. The second stage will take this intermediate result and produce the final sum output. Use registers to store the intermediate results and a clock to control the pipelining.

Design a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queue that can store 4-bit data. The FIFO should have the following inputs: `clk` (clock), `reset` (active high), `push` (to add data), `pop` (to remove data), and `data_in` (4-bit input data). The outputs should include `data_out` (4-bit output data) and `empty` (indicates if the FIFO is empty). The FIFO should support basic push and pop operations.

Design a Verilog module that performs bilinear interpolation on a 2x2 grid of input pixels. The module takes four 8-bit pixel values as inputs (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) and outputs the interpolated pixel value as an 8-bit output. The bilinear interpolation formula is given by:
```
f(x, y) = (1-x)*(1-y)*Q11 + x*(1-y)*Q12 + (1-x)*y*Q21 + x*y*Q22
```
where Q11, Q12, Q21, and Q22 are the pixel values, and x and y are the fractional parts of the coordinates (0 ≤ x, y < 1). The output should be rounded to the nearest integer.

Design a divide-by-4 circuit. The circuit should take a binary input and output a binary value that represents the input divided by 4. The circuit should work as a synchronous counter, incrementing the division result on every clock cycle. The input is a 4-bit binary number.
code:
module divide_by_4 (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [3:0] in,
    output reg [1:0] out
);
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            out <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            out <= in[3:2]; // Divide by 4: take the two most significant bits
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 4-bit Kogge-Stone adder that takes two 4-bit inputs A and B and produces a 4-bit sum S and a carry-out signal Cout.

Design an 8-bit SRAM cell with write and read functionality. The cell should have inputs for data (8 bits), write enable (1 bit), and output for the stored data (8 bits). When write enable is high, the input data should be stored in the SRAM cell. When write enable is low, the stored data should be output.

Design an SR latch using Verilog. The SR latch should have two inputs, S (set) and R (reset), and two outputs, Q and Qn (not Q). The outputs should hold their state until the inputs change. When S is high and R is low, Q should be set to high. When S is low and R is high, Q should be reset to low. Both S and R being high is an invalid state and should be avoided. The latch should remember its state between input changes.

Design a 2-channel DMA controller that can transfer data from memory to two different peripheral devices. The DMA controller should have the following specifications:
- Two channels with enable signals (`chan1_en`, `chan2_en`).
- Each channel has a memory address (`chan1_addr`, `chan2_addr`) and a data bus to transfer data (`data_out`).
- A control signal (`start`) initiates the DMA transfer for the enabled channel.
- The controller should complete the transfer in one clock cycle for each channel when enabled.
- A done signal (`done`) indicates that the transfer for the enabled channel is complete.
code:
module dma_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire chan1_en,
    input wire chan2_en,
    input wire [7:0] chan1_addr,
    input wire [7:0] chan2_addr,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg done
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            data_out <= 8'b0;
            done <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (chan1_en) begin
                data_out <= chan1_addr; // Simulate data transfer
                done <= 1'b1;
            end else if (chan2_en) begin
                data_out <= chan2_addr; // Simulate data transfer
                done <= 1'b1;
            end else begin
                done <= 1'b0;
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a DVFS controller that takes a temperature input and outputs the corresponding voltage and frequency settings. If the temperature is below 30 degrees Celsius, set voltage to 1.0V and frequency to 1.0GHz. If the temperature is between 30 and 70 degrees Celsius, set voltage to 0.9V and frequency to 900MHz. If the temperature is above 70 degrees Celsius, set voltage to 0.8V and frequency to 800MHz.
code:
module dvfs_controller (
    input [7:0] temperature,
    output reg [2:0] voltage, // 000: 1.0V, 001: 0.9V, 010: 0.8V
    output reg [2:0] frequency // 000: 1.0GHz, 001: 900MHz, 010: 800MHz
);
    
    always @(*) begin
        if (temperature < 30) begin
            voltage = 3'b000;    // 1.0V
            frequency = 3'b000;  // 1.0GHz
        end else if (temperature >= 30 && temperature <= 70) begin
            voltage = 3'b001;    // 0.9V
            frequency = 3'b001;  // 900MHz
        end else begin
            voltage = 3'b010;    // 0.8V
            frequency = 3'b010;  // 800MHz
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a down counter that counts from a given value down to zero. The counter should have a clock input, a reset input, and a 4-bit output. The counter should decrement the output value on each clock cycle until it reaches zero. The reset input should set the counter back to the initial value.

Design a simple Ethernet MAC controller that processes incoming frames and generates a simple acknowledgment signal after processing each frame. The MAC controller should have a clock input, a reset input, an enable signal for frame processing, an incoming data input, and an output acknowledgment signal. module cache_lru (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] address, // 8-bit address input
    input wire read,          // read operation
    input wire write,         // write operation
    output reg hit,           // cache hit
    output reg [7:0] data_out // data output
);
    reg [7:0] cache [3:0];     // 4 lines of cache
    reg [1:0] lru_counter [3:0]; // Counter for LRU tracking
    reg [1:0] next_lru;        // Next line to replace
    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                cache[i] <= 8'b0;
                lru_counter[i] <= 2'b0;
            end
            hit <= 0;
            data_out <= 8'b0;
        end else begin
            hit <= 0;
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                if (cache[i] == address) begin
                    hit <= 1;
                    data_out <= cache[i]; // return data
                    lru_counter[i] <= 2'b00; // Reset the LRU counter
                end else begin
                    lru_counter[i] <= lru_counter[i] + 1; // Increment other counters
                end
            end

            if (write && !hit) begin
                // Find the least recently used line
                next_lru = 0;
                for (i = 1; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                    if (lru_counter[i] > lru_counter[next_lru]) begin
                        next_lru = i;
                    end
                end
                cache[next_lru] <= address; // Replace the LRU line
                lru_counter[next_lru] <= 2'b00; // Reset LRU counter
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

                dist[i][j] = weight_matrix[(i*3 + j) * 8 +: 8];
            end
        end
        
        // Floyd-Warshall algorithm
        for (k = 0; k < 3; k = k + 1) begin
            for (i = 0; i < 3; i = i + 1) begin
                for (j = 0; j < 3; j = j + 1) begin
                    if (dist[i][j] > dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]) begin
                        dist[i][j] = dist[i][k] + dist[k][j];
                    end
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Output the shortest paths matrix
        for (i = 0; i < 3; i = i + 1) begin
            for (j = 0; j < 3; j = j + 1) begin
                shortest_paths[(i*3 + j) * 8 +: 8] = dist[i][j];
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module sata_controller (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input start,
    input error,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: IDLE, 01: TRANSFER, 10: ERROR
);
    
    // State encoding
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, TRANSFER = 2'b01, ERROR = 2'b10;

    // State transition
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= TRANSFER;
                    end
                end
                TRANSFER: begin
                    if (error) begin
                        state <= ERROR;
                    end else begin
                        // continue transferring
                        state <= TRANSFER;
                    end
                end
                ERROR: begin
                    if (~error) begin
                        state <= IDLE; // return to IDLE after error is cleared
                    end
                end
                default: state <= IDLE;
            endcase
        end
    end
